act1_quiz.prompt: Upper Nile communities rely on agropastoral and flood-recession livelihoods along the White Nile and Sobat, and the region enters 2021 after several years of exceptional flooding. Why does this history make a forecast rainfall deficit more worrying, not less?
act1_quiz.hint: Consider the state of grazing land and household reserves at the start of the season.
options: Prolonged flooding has already degraded dry-season grazing and cropland, so households face the deficit with depleted reserves and reduced coping capacity
Flooding leaves so much stored water that drought cannot develop afterwards
Flood-recession farming is unaffected by rainfall variability
Past floods mean the next season is statistically guaranteed to be wet
act1_quiz.correct: Prolonged flooding has already degraded dry-season grazing and cropland, so households face the deficit with depleted reserves and reduced coping capacity
act1_quiz.answer_note: Prolonged inundation damages floodplain pasture and dry-season grazing areas and disrupts cultivation, while households exhaust assets coping with floods and conflict stress. A below-normal rainy season then lands on a system with little buffer, so the same meteorological deficit produces a larger food-security risk.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Vulnerability context: the same hazard evidence implies higher risk when exposure and coping capacity are already eroded.

act1_quiz.prompt: Which rainy season is most critical for sorghum cultivation and pasture regeneration in Upper Nile, and roughly when does it fall?
act1_quiz.hint: South Sudan lies north of the equator with one main wet season.
options: A single main wet season from roughly May/June to October
Two short equatorial seasons centred on January and July
A winter rainfall season from December to February
Rainfall is uniform year-round in this part of the Nile basin
act1_quiz.correct: A single main wet season from roughly May/June to October
act1_quiz.answer_note: Upper Nile has one main rainy season, broadly May/June to October, which drives sorghum planting and pasture regeneration. A forecast deficit aimed at this window threatens the year's entire production cycle, which is why the mid-2021 event window matters so much.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Seasonal-calendar context for timing the forecast-deficit evidence against the livelihood-critical window.

decision.checkpoint_prompt: Forecast deficit and CDI agree months ahead of the event window. This is a STRONG, early signal. What DOC level do you set, and what anticipatory action does the ~6-month lead justify?

counterfactual.prompt: What if anticipatory action (anticipatory food/cash support and water-source protection) were triggered at the lead round on the strong forecast signal?
counterfactual.narrative: Slow-onset droughts give long lead. The counterfactual shows the loss-reduction value of acting on a confident seasonal signal rather than waiting for impact confirmation.
